land.text: Tirhut or Mithila in Bihar, with the Simraungadh country on the Nepal border

predecessors.note: The pages opened do not name the previous holder of Mithila; the Palas ruled Gauda and Vanga, which the Karnats and Senas both "coveted". Cliopatria's Pala Empire row is the nearest state.

land.text: Tirhut or Mithila in Bihar, with the Simraungadh country on the Nepal border

successors.note: 1324: "Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq turned his attention towards Bengal"; Harisimhadeva "fled northwards into what is now Nepal". The Karnats held parts of the region "up to the 15th century" beside the Oiniwar dynasty of central Mithila.

capitals.name: Nanapura (Champaran)
capitals.note: Nanyadeva's "original stronghold was Nanapura in Champaran district" (before Simraungadh); coordinates approximate.

capitals.name: Simraungadh
capitals.note: Infobox: Simraungadh after 1097, Darbhanga second capital (moved by Gangadeva after 1147); Simraungarh fort fled in 1324. Coordinates approximate (Bara district, Nepal).

correction.text: Tirhut or Mithila in Bihar, with the Simraungadh country on the Nepal border

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Karnat row). The page: the dynasty "controlled the areas we today know as Tirhut or Mithila in Bihar"; "almost full sovereignty from 1097 until 1324". Parts of Mithila later fell under Sena control and were regained by Gangadeva (Nanyadeva page, undated). No area given; the 100 km radius round Muzaffarpur plus the Simraungadh country is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Tirhut or Mithila in Bihar, with the Simraungadh country on the Nepal border

ledger.note: 10 July 1097: Nanyadeva takes the land at Simraungadh. an inscribed pillar at Simraungadh records that "king Nānyadeva took the land" in the Śaka year 1019, equated by the page with 10 July 1097; the dynasty was "established in 1097 CE by Nanyadeva". The page does not say who held Mithila before.

region.text: Tirhut or Mithila in Bihar, with the Simraungadh country on the Nepal border

ledger.note: 1324: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq enters Tirhut. "In 1324 CE, the founder of the Tughlaq dynasty and Sultan of Delhi, Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq, turned his attention towards Bengal"; "The king Harisimhadeva fled northwards into what is now Nepal" when an army approached Simraungarh.

region.text: Tirhut or Mithila in Bihar, with the Simraungadh country on the Nepal border

ledger.note: 1324: the Karnat kingdom of Mithila ends. "almost full sovereignty from 1097 until 1324"; Harisimhadeva (r. 1295-1324) was "the last Karnat sovereign of Tirhut", though Karnat rulers held parts of the region into the 15th century.

wars.name: Karnat-Sena conflict over Gauda and Mithila
wars.outcome: The Karnats and Senas "coveted the Pala territories of Gauda and Vanga"; "the Senas coming out victorious as per the Deopara inscription"; parts of Mithila later fell under Sena control and were regained by Gangadeva.
wars.note: The page gives no year for the Sena fight; the span is Nanyadeva's reign. Gangadeva invaded Gauda "at some point after 1147 CE" (Karnat page).

wars.name: Tughluq conquest of Tirhut

zones.text: Tirhut or Mithila in Bihar, with the Simraungadh country on the Nepal border

wars.outcome: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq advanced on Simraungarh while marching on Bengal; Harisimhadeva fled into Nepal.

certainty.note: No frontier is given; Tirhut / Mithila is the only land the pages name.

sources.title: Nanyadeva
sources.note: 10 July 1097; capital; Sena conflict; Nepal raids undated.

notes: Cliopatria has no Karnat row. Two pages. The Thakuri dossier's page says the Karnat Nanyadeva attacked Nuwakot; this page says Nepalese traditions assert attacks into the Kathmandu Valley, undated, aimed at loot. The infobox end is 1324; a citation title uses 1325. Gazetteer lacks Simraungadh, Darbhanga, Tirhut/Mithila, Nanapura; radii stand in. Counterparts needing a dossier: sena-dynasty already exists in Cliopatria (1072-1235).
